discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall state, and they identified the Z2 topological invariant that separates it from an ordinary insulator. Molenkamp's group then observed quantised edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, confirming the prediction by precise transport measurements. Together this work set up the field of topological insulators, which has since grown to include three-dimensional topological insulators, topological superconductivity, and magnetic topological phases. The field made possible the quantum anomalous Hall effect and axion-insulator states in magnetically doped and intrinsic magnetic materials such as MnBi2Te4. It is a model of close theory-experiment dialogue: an abstract topological invariant turned into a robust, quantised transport signature measured in the laboratory. It changed how we classify phases of electronic matter and opened routes to dissipationless electronics and topological quantum computation.
